01 / THE POINT

Less digital. More analogue.

Technology isn’t the enemy. It just doesn’t get the best seat for a week.

We don’t offer answers. We create an environment where you might find your own direction through doing, talking, listening, and living alongside other people.

DIGITAL
ANALOGUE

02 / A DAY AT CAMP

The daily rhythm

A rhythm, not a packed schedule.

There is time to learn something useful, and time to do absolutely nothing.

  1. Morning

    Wake slowly

    Share breakfast. Drink coffee. Check the weather. No morning scroll required.

    begin here
  2. Morning

    Use your hands or your head

    A practical workshop, a debate, or both. Learn from mentors, moderators, locals, and one another.

  3. Lunch

    Local food, cooked fresh

    A local cook prepares simple regional dishes, the kind of generous food a Romanian grandmother might put on the table.

  4. Afternoon

    Nothing is scheduled

    Read. Sleep. Walk. Play cards. Help in the garden. Have a ridiculous conversation, or an important one.

    BOREDOM
    ALLOWED
  5. Evening

    Cook, then gather

    Everyone helps prepare dinner and look after camp. Then come the fire, games, music, conversation, and stars.

04 / THE MOUNTAIN NIGHT

Leave from camp. On foot.

Carry it in.
Sleep under stars.
Walk home.

One night in the mountains, reached under your own power. A real challenge with experienced leadership, thoughtful planning, and proper equipment, not survival training.

PHONES DOWN

Phones are stored safely and remain available when needed. Use a digital camera, take the memory card home.

A REAL VILLAGE

A simple base in a living rural community, connected to local food, craft, and knowledge.

SAFETY NOTE / 001

The experience includes hiking, outdoor living, and intentional discomfort. Appropriate equipment, planning, and experienced leadership are fundamental. Full eligibility, accessibility, and safety details will come with pilot registration.

06 / ASK US

Useful questions

Before you pack.

Can I use my phone, and can home reach me?+

Phones are stored safely for most of the week. There are times to contact home, and the camp remains reachable in an emergency.

Do I need hiking or camping experience?+

The pilot is designed around learning by doing, but final experience and fitness requirements will be shared before applications open.

Is this survival training, and what is provided?+

No. It is a planned challenge with experienced leadership. Backpacks, reliable tents, and sleeping bags suitable for temperatures around 0°C are planned.

When is it, and how much will it cost?+

Dates and pricing are not set yet. Join the pilot list and we’ll share them when the first week is ready.
